---
title: DateParts
description: "Recurring calendar patterns from a timestamp, such as weekday and hour."
---

`DateParts` represents recurring calendar patterns from a timestamp. In this
payment example, `booked_at` supplies the weekday and hour as context for
predicting a later dispute. Whether those patterns help is a question for
held-out evaluation. The [transaction sequence](../learn/add-transaction-history.qmd)
uses this field on every transaction, including the latest one. Calendar
cycles and sequence order supply different evidence; neither is an exact
elapsed duration.

```python
import relflow as rf

model = rf.Model.xs(
    amount=rf.Number,
    merchant=rf.Category,
    booked_at=rf.DateParts(dateparts=["day_of_week", "hour_of_day"]),
    disputed=rf.Boolean(mask=True),
)
```

One labeled payment:

```yaml
amount: 84.50
merchant: North Market
booked_at: "2026-05-28T14:30:45"
disputed: false
```

## Input and options

Accepts Arrow date, timestamp, or string values. Strings are parsed by Arrow
using `pattern` when supplied; otherwise Arrow casts them to timestamps.
Calendar extraction uses second-resolution timestamps. Naive timestamps are
read as wall-clock time, and zone-aware timestamps are read in their own zone,
so `hour_of_day` and `day_of_week` describe local time. Strings that carry an
offset are normalized to UTC by Arrow before parts are taken; give such
columns a zone upstream instead.

| Option | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `dateparts` | required | Nonempty, unique list of parts; casing and separators are normalized. |
| `pattern` | `None` | Optional strptime-style format for Arrow string parsing. |
| `jitter` | `rf.Jitter()` | Training noise on the generated sine/cosine coordinates. |

| Part | Period |
| --- | ---: |
| `day_of_year` | 366 |
| `week_of_year` | 53 |
| `month_of_year` | 12 |
| `day_of_month` | 31 |
| `week_of_month` | 6 |
| `day_of_week` | 7 |
| `hour_of_day` | 24 |
| `minute_of_hour` | 60 |
| `second_of_minute` | 60 |

## Representation and output

Each part becomes a sine/cosine pair: the end of a cycle is near its beginning.
relflow projects each pair and combines the results with a state embedding.
Null, padded, and masked content is zero; state remains separate.

[Jitter](../reference/jitter.qmd) changes the circle coordinates, not the
timestamp, and does not renormalize noisy pairs. Its magnitude is measured in
coordinate units. Both settings of `jitter.normalize` use this same boundary.

Reconstruction learns state cross entropy and mean per-part cosine distance.
The per-part `mae` metric is angular error in radians, not elapsed time.

DateParts has no decoded public content and does not generate timestamps.
Use `embed=True` for a contextual embedding; see
[shared leaf options](index.qmd#shared-leaf-options).

The [month-inference evidence](../evidence/temporal/month-from-day-of-year.html)
tests a recurring relationship on withheld dates and years. The
[leap-boundary evidence](../evidence/temporal/leap-boundary-requires-context.html)
shows how selecting too few calendar coordinates can make the answer ambiguous.
